item.title: [ZEPPELIN-6375] Websocket connection does not auto-reconnect on abnormal closure in new UI
item.description:
1. Problem:
    • The new UI lacks automatic WebSocket reconnection when connections are closed abnormally.
    • This differs from the classic UI which automatically reconnects on non-normal closures using the `reconnectIfNotNormalClose` flag.
  2. When this occurs:
    1. Server-side idle timeout (~30 seconds by default in Jetty WebSocket)
      • Even though client sends PING every 10 seconds, timeouts still occur
      • Particularly common in Kubernetes deployments with nginx ingress
    2. Browser tab inactive/background
      • Chrome throttles timers to 1 second minimum after 10 seconds of inactivity
      • After 5+ minutes, timers throttled to 1 minute intervals
      • PING interval (10s) becomes unreliable, causing server timeouts
    3. Computer sleep/suspend
      • JavaScript timers pause during system sleep
      • Server closes connection due to no activity
      • Connection not restored when system wakes
    4. Network interruptions or server restarts
  3. Current Behavior:
    • Connection permanently lost
    • No automatic reconnection attempt
    • Real-time updates stop (paragraph results, job status, etc.)
    • Users must manually refresh the page
  4. Contrast with Classic UI:
    • The old UI uses `angular-websocket` library with `reconnectIfNotNormalClose = true`, which automatically reconnects on any non-nomral closure (clos code !== 1000).
  5. Reproduction:
    1. Open notebook in new Angular UI
    2. Leave browser tab inactive for 2-3 minutes
    3. Return to tab
    4. Conection is dead, no auto-reconnect
item.summary: Websocket connection does not auto-reconnect on abnormal closure in new UI

https://github.com/apache/zeppelin/pull/5116

Hi there chanholee !

I've reviewed your changes, built the fixes for Zeppelin 12, and deployed them to our test environment in Kubernetes.

I've observed an issue with WebSocket reconnection in the new GUI: after a WebSocket disconnect (which occurs due to timeout), it successfully reconnects. However, after reconnection, it's impossible to re-run paragraphs on the already-opened notebook page, even when the interpreter was previously running successfully.

Important observations:

GUI-specific issue: This problem only manifests in the new GUI. The classic GUI works correctly - after WebSocket reconnection, paragraph execution continues to work normally.

Service architecture: We're using a LoadBalancer service in Kubernetes, which might be relevant for WebSocket session persistence.

Workaround: If I refresh the entire page after reconnection, everything returns to normal functionality in the new GUI.

Reproduction Steps (New GUI only):

1) Open notebook in new GUI interface

2) Wait 5+ minutes (WebSocket times out)

3) System reconnects automatically

4) Try to run any paragraph → No response/failure

5) Refresh page (Ctrl+F5) in new GUI → Everything works again

This appears to be a state synchronization issue where the reconnected session loses reference to the active notebook context. The NPE suggests the notebook object becomes unreachable after reconnection, despite the UI showing it as open.

Could you please look into this reconnection/state restoration logic? Let me know if you need additional logs or reproduction details.

Thanks!

Thanks for the detailed report pavelsha141992 !

I checked your reproduction case and confirmed that the new GUI was not reloading the note data after a WebSocket reconnection (it only fetched the data during the initial page load).

I've opened a PR that addresses the issue: https://github.com/apache/zeppelin/pull/5129

If you have some time, it would be great if you could take a look and verify that it resolves the problem on you end as well.

Thanks again for reporting this bug!

Hello chanholee ! Thank you very much for your prompt response.

I've made the changes you suggested for my Zeppelin notebook, and the issue I described earlier is gone. Now, after the WebSocket reconnects, I can continue working with notebook paragraphs and re-execute them.

However, after 5-10 minutes of working in the notebook, an endless cycle of WebSocket reconnections begins, leading to visual bugs like the ones shown in the attached video.

...and then the browser completely froze and displayed this:

Unfortunately, there are no related error messages in the server logs to help diagnose this.

Thanks you!
chanholee Hi! It seems my problem with the zeppelin is more complicated than I thought

pavelsha141992 

Sorry that I couldn't spend more time on thie earlier. Things have been a bit busy recently.

I found that some resources were not being cleaned up properly during the WebSocket reconnection process, so I added an additional commit to the existing PR:
https://github.com/apache/zeppelin/pull/5129

Since I cannot reproduce the K8S launcher environment on my machine, I tested by simulating a WebSocket disconnection in Chrome DevTools instead.
In the Network tab, I switched from "No throttling" to "Offline" to mimic a broken WebSocket connection without restarting the server.

With the earlier commits (including the one around the time you first reported the issue and the previous fix commit), I was able to reproduce the strange behavior.
However, with the latest commit I just pushed, the issue no longer occurs on my side.
The WebSocket reconnects successfully, and I can immediately execute paragraphs afterward.

Could you please check if this also resolves the issue on your side?

Thanks!

chanholee 
Oh, thank you so much! Now I don't see any problems. It's just great!
I really hope that these fixes will be included in version 13 and that this will help other users.
